acceptance: A test that leaves a third-party logger level changed is restored or reported by the guard (regression test)
The root logger handler count is unchanged after tests/integration/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py
Median per-test overhead of the guard is measured and is at most 1 ms
The serial order docs-contract tests then sqlite engine-version tests passes
context: Found 2026-11-26 by a per-test logger-state watch over the first 606 preflight test files of the corpus rule branch.
description:
## Problem
scripts/docs_data_sources.py set `logging.getLogger("sqlglot").setLevel(logging.ERROR)` at import time (since #3545). tests/unit/scripts/test_doc_contracts.py imports it through its module fixture, so in a serial run every later test lost sqlglot warnings, and tests/unit/utils/test_sqlite_engine_version.py::test_other_unsupported_messages_keep_warning_behaviour failed (4 cases) only in preflight order. The import-time call is fixed in the corpus rule PR (commit 5c63a58be0: the docs export quiets sqlglot only while it runs).

The guards meant to catch such leaks did not: tests/conftest.py::_restore_logging_state and tests/utilities/module_state_guard.py restore only `benchbox*` and `mcp.server.transport_security` loggers. A per-test watch also showed tests/integration/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py::test_two_worker_submission_observation_and_completion raising the root logger's handler count from 2 to 4 without restoring it.

## Change
- Extend the logging-state guard to cover the root logger's handlers and level and any other logger whose level, propagate flag, disabled flag or handlers a test changes, restoring them or failing the leaking test.
- Fix the durable-jobs handler leak at its source.

## Decision gates
- A product module that changes a third-party logger at import time is a product defect: report and fix it, never let the guard hide it.
- Measure the guard's per-test overhead; if the median exceeds 1 ms, restrict it to a cheap diff of changed loggers and re-measure; if it still exceeds 1 ms, stop and report.

## Verification rubric
- A regression test sets a third-party logger level without restoring it and shows the guard restores or reports it.
- After the durable-jobs test the root handler count equals its value before the test.

## Guardrails
- Reproduce or measure before changing anything; record the command, log path and run id in the item context.
- Fix the root cause. Never skip, xfail, loosen a check or bound, or raise a timeout only to make a test or run pass; a timing or limit change needs measured evidence and owner approval.
- No rule, check, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix unless the item is about that platform.
- Never edit stored result files under results-data/ or CHANGELOG.md; user-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; reuse existing helpers.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. Never touch the lock or set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off, or raise BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB. No live cloud runs.
- Work in a linked worktree; one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. No stand-in approval unless the owner names the PR and head.
- Re-read paths and line numbers before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- When a decision gate's stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner with the evidence; never substitute a different decision.
